'''Henna L. L. Koivusalo''' (born 1985) is a Finnish mathematician who works in the UK as a lecturer at the School of Mathematics of the [[University of Bristol]].{{r|cv}} Her research involves [[dynamical system]]s, [[fractal geometry]], [[Diophantine approximation]], and the cut-and-project method for generating [[aperiodic tiling]]s and [[quasicrystal]]s.{{r|bennett}}

==Education and career==
Koivusalo received bachelor's and master's degrees in mathematics from the [[University of Jyväskylä]] in 2009. She went on to doctoral study in mathematics at the [[University of Oulu]], and completed her Ph.D. in 2013.{{r|cv}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Dimensions of random fractals'', was jointly supervised by Esa and [[Maarit Järvenpää]].{{r|mg}}

She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of York]] from 2013 to 2016, and from 2016 to 2020 worked towards a [[habilitation]] at the [[University of Vienna]]. She has been a lecturer at the University of Bristol since 2020.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Koivusalo is the 2025 recipient of the [[Anne Bennett Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]], awarded "for her work on cut-and-project sets, dynamical systems and fractals and her dedication to the advancement of women in mathematics".{{r|bennett}}
